sections.h2: Where is Westminster, Colorado, and which counties does it cover?
sections.html:
Westminster is a home rule city in western Adams County and northeastern Jefferson County, about 9 miles north-northwest of the Colorado State Capitol in Denver. At the 2020 Census, 71,240 of its 116,317 residents lived in Adams County and 45,077 lived in Jefferson County.

That split is the first thing to check when you sell. The county your house sits in decides which treasurer sends your tax bill, which clerk records your deed and which assessor sets your value. Westminster borders Broomfield to the north, Thornton to the northeast, Northglenn and Federal Heights to the east, and Arvada to the south.

The city covers about 33.9 square miles at 5,325 feet of elevation and is the eighth most populous city in Colorado.

sections.h2: What is the history behind Westminster's older neighborhoods?
sections.html:
Westminster began with a Kentucky farmer, Pleasant DeSpain, who built a home in 1870 on 160 acres near what is now West 76th Avenue and Lowell Street. The area was called DeSpain Junction, then Harris after a Connecticut developer, C.J. Harris, bought farms there in 1885 and sold them in small tracts to fruit farmers.

In 1890 the Denver Presbytery agreed to build a university on land in Harris. Classes started in 1908 at Westminster University of Colorado, sometimes called the Princeton of the West, and the post office took the Westminster name the same year. The school stopped operating in 1917, and the red sandstone building, known as Westminster Castle, is on the National Register of Historic Places. The 1881 Bowles House is also listed.

Westminster grew slowly until the 1950s and then quickly: 1,686 people in 1950, 13,850 in 1960, 50,211 in 1980 and 100,940 in 2000. The city's own rental code says it exists to address the deterioration of the city's aging rental housing, which fits a place that added most of its population from 1950 on.

Ball Corporation was the largest primary employer in Westminster in 2019, with 1,252 employees, according to the city's economic development list as compiled on its Wikipedia page.

sections.h2: How do roads and transit connect Westminster to Denver and Boulder?
sections.html:
Westminster is crossed by Interstate 25, US 36, US 287 and State Highways 95, 121 and 128. US 36 links it to both Denver and Boulder.

  • RTD's Flatiron Flyer bus rapid transit runs in the US 36 express lanes toward Boulder and Denver.
  • The Westminster Center Park-n-Ride sits on both sides of US 36 across Sheridan Boulevard from the site, with about 1,546 weekday boardings and about 498 buses per day.
  • The B Line opened in 2016, with about 6 miles of commuter rail from Westminster Station to Denver Union Station.
  • Denver International Airport and Rocky Mountain Metropolitan Airport are the nearby airports.

A house within a short drive of the B Line or the park-n-ride gives a buyer an easy commute, and sellers in those areas can use that in their own conversations with a buyer.

sections.h2: What are Westminster's rental licensing and inspection rules?
sections.html:
Every residential rental property in Westminster must be licensed or registered under the city's Rental Code, which matters if you own a house you rent out and want to sell it.

The program draws a line between larger and smaller rentals, according to the city's Rental Property Inspections page.

  • Properties with four or more units, or four or more rental dwellings under one owner in a townhome or condo community, need a license.
  • License fees are $50 per rental property, and inspection fees are $40 per unit, or $20 per income-restricted unit.
  • Single-family houses, duplexes and up to three townhomes or condos under one owner need registration only, with no fee and no required inspection.
  • Systematic inspections apply to residential rentals six years old or older that have four or more units.
  • Single-family and duplex rentals are inspected on a complaint basis, or proactively if the owner asks.

If you are selling a tenant-occupied Westminster house, confirm registration is current. The city's rental property line is 303-706-3026. You can read the program details on the City of Westminster Rental Property Inspections page.

sections.h2: When are property taxes due in Adams County and Jefferson County?
sections.html:
Both counties use the same Colorado schedule: a half payment by the last day of February, a second half by June 15, or a full payment by April 30. Both also collect taxes in arrears, which means each year's bill covers the previous year.

Jefferson County's Treasurer is at 100 Jefferson County Parkway in Golden and is open Monday to Thursday and closed Fridays. Look at the top of your bill to see which county sent it. The Adams page is the Adams County due dates page, and Jefferson County's is its Important Dates page.

sections.h2: What parks and open space affect Westminster home values?
sections.html:
Westminster began preserving open space in 1985, when voters first approved a sales tax earmarked for acquiring and maintaining it. The city now owns more than 3,000 acres, including large areas in Standley Lake Regional Park and the Westminster Hills area.

The Big Dry Creek Trail runs about 12 miles from the city's eastern edge to Standley Lake, and other trails follow the Farmers' High Line Canal, Walnut Creek and Little Dry Creek. Downtown Westminster connects to the US 36 Bikeway, part of a trail system of more than 145 miles.

Downtown Westminster is a 105-acre redevelopment on the former Westminster Mall site, which was demolished in 2012. It includes an Alamo Drafthouse and a 125-room hotel, with plans for about 2,300 multifamily, condo and townhouse units. The Orchard Town Center, an outdoor mall, is at I-25 and 144th Avenue.

sections.h2: Which schools are in or near Westminster?
sections.html: High schools in or near Westminster include Westminster High School, Standley Lake High School, Mountain Range High School, Pomona High School, Legacy High School, Northglenn High School, Jefferson Academy High School, Hidden Lake High School and the Academy of Charter Schools. Adams County School District 50 opened a new Westminster High School in 2010, replacing the old one and Ranum High School. Shepherd of the Valley Lutheran School serves preschool through eighth grade.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work for a Westminster homeowner?
sections.html:
A cash buyer purchases the house without a lender, so the closing does not depend on a loan approval. You receive an offer, decide whether it works, and set a closing date with the title company.

That fits owners with a tenant-occupied house, an inherited property, or a home that needs work, and it avoids a long list of repairs before showing. Westminster sellers usually reach us after a job transfer, an inheritance, or a house that has sat vacant. If the house is a rental, settle the registration first so the title company has no surprises.

faqs.q: Is Westminster in Adams County or Jefferson County?
faqs.a: Both. Westminster is in western Adams County and northeastern Jefferson County. At the 2020 Census, 71,240 residents lived in the Adams County part and 45,077 in the Jefferson County part.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental license to sell a rented house in Westminster?
faqs.a: You need the rental to be properly licensed or registered while you own it. Single-family houses, duplexes and up to three condos or townhomes under one owner are registered at no fee. Properties with four or more units are licensed at $50 per property, plus $40 per unit for inspection.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Westminster?
faqs.a: The first half is due by the end of February, the full amount by April 30 and the second half by June 15. Check whether your bill came from Adams or Jefferson County.
The RTD B Line opened in 2016 and runs about 6 miles of commuter rail between Westminster Station and Denver Union Station.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Westminster house with repair needs?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer takes the house as-is, so you do not need to fix the roof, flooring or fixtures before closing.
